_comment: AER-679 moving-position pass threshold, narrowed by AER-1082, SVS provenance corrected by AER-1086. svs.frame_gap_ms.p95 stays gated at 50 ms == PROBE_GAP_WARN_MS (map/perf.py). The bar's old justification cited a DEMO-era figure (bench demo pattern swept ALT continuously with LAT/LONG pinned -- the exact regime AER-677 retired) and should never have sourced a live gate. AER-1086 re-measured on healthy current dev with the moving-position harness itself (--target svs, 130 kt/280 deg/20 Hz, 41 s, real GL via a shared X display -- offscreen QPA can't create a QOpenGLWidget context at all): p50 33.0 / p95 34.0 / p99 34.9 / max 35.6 ms, comfortably under 50 ms with collector hit rates >99% (frame_total_ms stayed ~4.6-5.0 ms, so the render itself is cheap, not starved). This also kills the suspected 'floored at the 20 Hz drive period' mechanism: SVS repaints on its own free-running 30 fps QTimer (ai/__init__.py set_frame_rate, default), not on position change, so the ~33 ms gap tracks that timer's nominal 33.3 ms period, not the 50 ms drive period. 50 ms therefore keeps clean margin (~16 ms) above the real healthy baseline. map.frame_gap_ms.p95 is NOT gated: AER-692 showed it is dominated by pose-quantization arithmetic (10 NM half-range, 130 kt -> ~266 ms to cross the half-pixel the pose gate requires, then a 10 Hz frame-clock boundary on top), so ~300 ms is the CORRECT designed answer for that scenario and a 50 ms bound on it is always-red regardless of code health. The map is instead gated on map.probe.p95_ms -- GuiProbe's own tick-to-tick wall-clock gap against its 10 ms timer, the objective GIL-starvation detector, insensitive to pose quantization (measured p50 9.7 / p95 10.9 / max 13.6 ms in the very run that read 205 ms of frame gap). 50 ms is PROBE_GAP_WARN_MS itself here, not borrowed. See docs/moving_map_spec.md section 9.2.
